items.summary: Delhi Police Special Cell's Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations unit apprehended a 14-year-old from Haryana accused of selling Agniveer (Indian Army soldier) recruitment data on the dark web. The boy allegedly used AI tools to steal candidate information from a Ministry of Home Affairs portal, and police recovered files for 2,500 individuals from his devices; they have sought verification from that ministry as the investigation continues.
items.title: Delhi police arrest 14-year-old for selling Agniveer recruitment data online

items.summary: The Narcotics Control Bureau busted an interstate pharmaceutical drug network that diverted legally manufactured prescription drugs for illicit sale from Delhi to Kashmir, arresting four individuals and uncovering an illegal storage facility in Shahdara. Recoveries included large quantities of codeine cough syrup plus tramadol, alprazolam, and nitrazepam tablets. A joint operation by Delhi Police with Jammu and Kashmir units is investigating links to Punjab, Bihar, and Uttar Pradesh, while the Ministry of Home Affairs weighs in on the case.
items.title: Narcotics Control Bureau busts Delhi-to-Kashmir drug network, arrests four

items.summary: Economists Santosh Mehrotra and Mitali Nikore argue that Prime Minister Narendra Modi's November 19 remarks urging businesses to boost manufacturing, job creation, wage growth, and product quality are unlikely to change corporate behaviour on their own. Responding at the FICCI centenary convention in New Delhi where he criticised Indian corporates for benefiting from government incentives without adequately contributing to wealth distribution or employment, Mehrotra said investors respond to economic demand rather than political exhortation: "Investors and big corporates do not start investing and creating jobs simply because the Prime Minister or Finance Minister exhorts them to do so; they respond to whether there is demand in the economy." Nikore stressed that structural barriers must be addressed, noting a policy gap in which the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme tied government support to employment targets while corporate tax cuts were granted without such conditions. Mehrotra outlined three immediate priorities: reviving micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), which he said have struggled since demonetisation; giving employers a direct stake in vocational skilling rather than blaming workers for skill gaps; and increasing corporate investment in research and development (R&D).
items.title: Economists say Modi's appeal to Indian corporates won't drive investment or jobs

items.summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis directed MIDC to prepare a proposal for a wholly owned subsidiary that would distribute both treated wastewater from municipal sewage treatment plants and conventional water to industrial units and data centres, consolidating the operation and maintenance of treatment facilities with industrial water supply. The move responds to drought conditions across the state and rising concerns about the electricity and water demands of data centres, which prompted the formation of a 17-member committee led by former Atomic Energy Commission chairman Anil Kakodkar to assess their environmental and infrastructure effects within three months. Fadnavis also called for long-term water plans covering population growth and industrial demand: Mumbai Metropolitan Region up to 2051, where current population is about [q3: 2.75 crore] could require [q4: 16,139 million litres] a day by that date; Pune Metropolitan Region up to 2047, where population around [q5: 1.8 crore] is projected to reach [q6: 4.12 crore], with current water allocation of [q7: 36.90 TMC] against demand of [q8: 41.65 TMC] and a requirement expected to reach about [q9: 100 TMC].
items.title: Maharashtra plans dedicated water supply company for data centres amid drought

items.summary: On Monday the Supreme Court ordered every state government to forthwith constitute a grievance committee in compliance with Rule 5(6)(b) of the Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017. The bench of justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi issued the order while disposing a batch of petitions filed by birder Anand Arya, advocate MK Balakrishnan, and NGO Vanashakti seeking demarcation and preservation of wetlands; they argued that nine years after the 2017 Rules came into force states have failed to demarcate them. The committee is required under Rule 5(6)(b) to consist of four members, hear public grievances about encroachment, forward those grievances to State Wetland Authorities within 90 days of the Rules becoming operational, and help ensure protection of wetlands identified by the Space Application Centre (SAC) Atlas 2021. The bench directed copies be sent to all chief secretaries for immediate implementation and posted the matter for further hearing on December 2. This order continues a series of directives: in October the court held that water bodies fall within Article 21 as sources of drinking water, last month it ordered ground truthing of non-wetland water bodies, and in December 2024 it directed states to demarcate all wetlands from the 2021 SAC Atlas within three months—a deadline pushed at states' request. Per a Centre report submitted last year, out of the 231,195 wetlands inventoried in the 2021 SAC Atlas ground-truthing is complete for nearly 80% and boundary demarcation has been completed for close to 95,000; MoEFCC currently lists 1,319 notified wetlands and 103 Ramsar sites. The court noted that the atlas also identified some 555,557 smaller wetlands (less than 2.25 hectares) needing protection steps.
items.title: Supreme Court directs all states to form wetland grievance committees under Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is set to inaugurate a six-lane, 9.76-km-long cable-stayed bridge across the Ganga in Vaishali district on Saturday, built at a cost of around ₹4,280 crore and named 'Nitish Setu' after former chief minister Nitish Kumar. The structure will connect Bidupur in Vaishali with Kachchi Dargah near Patna as part of a larger 19.7-km connectivity project linking NH-22 to NH-322, expected to ease traffic on the Mahatma Gandhi Setu and JP Setu while improving access for residents of Raghopur Diara and benefiting agricultural producers including litchi, banana, maize and vegetable growers. The naming has sparked a political dispute between the ruling BJP-JD(U) alliance and opposition RJD; RJD working president Tejashwi Yadav alleged the BJP was signalling that Kumar's career was over and claimed his party had earlier proposed naming it after freedom fighter Akshayvat Rai, while JD(U) leaders dismissed the demand. The project was first commissioned by Nitish Kumar in 2012, with construction beginning only in 2015.
items.title: PM Modi to inaugurate Nitish Setu bridge in Bihar

items.summary: In a Hyderabad interaction, Bollywood actor Salman Khan said he would readily accept film offers from Tollywood stars Chiranjeevi, Venkatesh, Ram Charan and Jr NTR if they approached him. He also joked that his favourite Telugu hero should be himself rather than naming one of the industry's leading actors. The remarks reflect existing cross-industry ties: Salman made a special appearance in Chiranjeevi's Godfather, while Ram Charan appeared in a cameo in Salman's Kisi Ka Bhai Kisi Ki Jaan, and he has shown admiration for Allu Arjun after the Hindi remake Seeti Maar of his film Radhe. The comments are statements of willingness rather than confirmed projects.
items.title: Salman Khan Says He Would Accept Telugu Film Offers From Chiranjeevi, Venkatesh, Ram Charan and Jr NTR

items.summary: National Investigation Agency Director General Rakesh Aggarwal told The Hindu that US citizen Matthew VanDyke and six Ukrainians, arrested in March for allegedly supplying weapons to ethnic armed groups hostile to India, have not been charged under the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act because investigators must first establish whether anyone they trained were Indian insurgents. They had filed a chargesheet on September 8 accusing all seven of immigration violations under the 2025 Immigration and Foreigners Act for entering on valid visas but travelling to Mizoram without a restricted area permit, meeting hostile groups in Myanmar, and receiving drone deliveries from Europe; though arrested under UAPA, only immigration offences were charged. A Delhi court granted them one month abroad starting September 24, then extended permission until February after the agency requested more time for its probe. Aggarwal said charges would follow once Indian insurgent identities are confirmed, that legal remedies would be pursued if VanDyke fails to return for trial, and he denied custodial torture claims by citing six court appearances without complaint.
items.title: NIA chief says terror charges cannot be invoked against VanDyke until Indian insurgents are identified

items.summary: The FBI placed fugitive Satinderjeet Singh, aka Goldy Brar, on its Ten Most Wanted Fugitives list and announced a reward of up to [q1: $1 million] for information leading to his arrest. He is wanted for allegedly heading the North American operations of the Lawrence Bishnoi Organised Crime Group (OCG), which the FBI alleges is headquartered in India with thousands of members across North America, Europe, and Australia. Brar faces charges including RICO conspiracy, extortion conspiracies, and drug distribution conspiracies after a federal arrest warrant was issued against him on July 1 by the US District Court in Los Angeles.
items.title: FBI adds Goldy Brar to Ten Most Wanted list with $1 million reward

items.summary: A suspected mass methanol-poisoning incident struck the Chakpi Karong area of Manipur's Chandel district after residents consumed a locally made alcoholic drink. Shija Hospital Joint Managing Director Dr. Chetan Khundongbam reported receiving 140 patients, one of whom arrived dead and had already expired; three more were critical and undergoing hemodialysis as of the report. The hospital described its prepared beds as overwhelmed and requested help from the state health department, RIMS, and JNIMS to refer additional cases. Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand visited the facility to meet patients and assure government support, while Chandel district administration issued a public warning urging residents to avoid beverages from doubtful sources.
items.title: Suspected methanol poisoning in Manipur's Chandel district killed at least 15 people and hospitalised nearly 150.
